chapters.title: Subscriptions: the whole lifecycle
chapters.subtitle: From first payment to the last

steps.text: A subscription starts, renews, fails, pauses and ends. This video shows the statuses, how to pause, resume and cancel a subscription, what a subscriber sees, and how to end a membership early.

chapters.title: Why a lifecycle
chapters.subtitle: From first payment to the last

steps.text: A subscription is not one sale. It starts, renews, sometimes fails to renew, gets paused, and one day ends.
Each of those moments decides whether the subscriber has access, and whether they are billed.
You see every subscription in one place, with its status and its history, and you can pause it, resume it, or cancel it.
Subscribers manage their own plans from My account, and memberships can be ended early.

chapters.title: The statuses
chapters.subtitle: Active, past due, paused, canceled, expired

steps.text: Active and Trial subscriptions are billed, and their subscribers have access.
Past due means a renewal payment failed. The subscriber keeps access through a grace period of seven days while the payment is retried.
Paused means billing was suspended by an administrator. Canceled means it was ended, and Expired means the grace period ran out or every billing cycle was billed.
When a subscription stops being current, the roles its plan gave are removed.
A plan is a product with a subscription part. Open it to see the billing duration, the limit on how many cycles are billed, and the trial days.
Under Member access, tick the roles the plan grants. The roles are added when the subscription becomes current, and removed when it stops being.
Open Subscriptions, Agreements, and click Manage on a subscription. It shows the owner, what is billed, its actions and its history.
Pause billing suspends billing without ending the subscription. Enter an optional reason, and confirm. The status becomes Paused, and Resume starts it again.
Cancel subscription ends it. Keep access until the paid period ends lets the subscriber use what they paid for. The history lists everything that happened, newest first.
A signed in subscriber sees their plans under My account, with the status, what they pay, and when it renews.
They can cancel a plan that is active, in a trial, or past due. The subscription ends when the paid period does, and the history says so.
A membership product, one that is bought once and puts its buyer in a role, is listed under Commerce, Memberships. Search by name, and filter by Active, Expired or Ended early.

End now ends a membership at once, and refunds nothing. The member loses what the membership opened for them. A membership sold as a subscription is managed under Subscriptions, Agreements, like the one in this video.
Subscription settings has whether guests can sign up without an account, the currency, and the roles a plan is allowed to give.
The grace period after a failed payment is seven days, and is not a setting on that page.
With Reports on, the subscription reports show new, active and canceled subscriptions, and what is due to renew.
With Workflows on, subscription events start workflows, for example to welcome a subscriber.
A holiday: pause billing, and resume it when they are back.
A cancellation: keep access until the paid period ends.
A failed card: the grace period gives the subscriber time to fix it.
A refunded member: end the membership now.
Follow every subscription, pause and resume billing, and end what should end. Thanks for watching.
